S1.why: "bez maksas" is the phrase Latvian stores print on free things and stands alone without a noun; "bezmaksas" would need one after it.

S2.why: An invitation in the polite jūs imperative, the form the vocabulary file uses; it asks the person to keep going and names no limit.

S3.s: Visas %lld bezmaksas vietas ir aizņemtas. Jūsu Cutlings arī turpmāk strādās bez maksas.
S3.back: All 5 free places are taken. Your Cutlings also henceforth will-work without charge.
S3.why: "vietas aizņemtas" is how Latvian says seats are taken, so nothing sounds like an error; the second sentence makes "free" and "keep working" one promise. "Cutlings" is the vocabulary's indeclinable plural.

S4.s: Pirmos %lld Cutlings varat saglabāt bez maksas.
S4.back: First 5 Cutlings you-can save without charge.
S4.why: The topic comes first and "bez maksas" last, where Latvian puts the new information; "Pirmos" is masculine accusative plural to agree with Cutlings.

S5.s: Jūsu Cutlings aizņem %1$lld no %2$lld bezmaksas vietām.
S5.back: Your Cutlings take-up 3 of 5 free places.
S5.why: The present-tense verb "aizņem" has one form for singular and plural, so the line is right for 1 used as well as 4; "no" takes the dative plural "vietām".

S6.why: A short noun headline, as Latvian row titles are; Cutlings is indeclinable, so the missing dative ending is not noticed.

S7.s: Varat saglabāt līdz %@ tekstiem un %lld attēliem.
S7.back: You-can save up-to 5000 texts and 500 images.
S7.why: "līdz" takes the dative in the plural (tekstiem, attēliem); the item kinds are the vocabulary's own words Teksts and Attēli.

S8.why: A Latvian list of three has one "un" and no comma before it; the product names keep Apple's spelling and the lowercase i.

S9.s: Viens pirkums der visās ierīcēs ar jūsu Apple kontu.
S9.back: One purchase is-valid in-all devices with your Apple account.
S9.why: "der" is what Latvians say of a ticket or a code that is valid; "Apple kontu" is the vocabulary's form.

S10.why: A plain statement to the person in the jūs form, with a verb; "vienreiz" already rules out anything recurring.

S11.why: One "bez" governs all three, which is how a Latvian would list absences; "reģistrēšanās" is the everyday word for signing up for an account.

S12.why: The infinitive command form and the wording Latvian iOS apps use for the App Store restore action.

S13.why: The present tense shows the work under way, the way Latvian progress labels read; it ends on the single ellipsis character.

S14.why: "atbloķēt" is the standard Latvian verb for unlock, in the infinitive as Latvian buttons are; "par" plus the price is the natural phrase, and "pay once" is already said by the row above.

S15.why: The same verb as S14 without the price, so the button keeps its word when the price arrives.

S16.why: What a Latvian says to put something off politely; "Ne tagad" sounds more like a refusal.

S17.why: The infinitive Latvian close buttons use.

S18.why: Short and warm, with "viss" covering the whole app and the new room; "jūsu" keeps the polite address.

S19.s: Paldies. Tā jūs atbalstāt Cutling un cilvēku, kas to veido viens pats.
S19.back: Thanks. That-way you support Cutling and the-person who it makes alone himself.
S19.why: "viens pats" says one person, alone, without the stiff "vienīgais izstrādātājs"; the masculine matches the app's maker. "tā" points back to the purchase just made.

S20.s: Prieks jūs atkal redzēt. Jūsu pirkums ir atjaunots.
S20.back: Joy you again to-see. Your purchase is restored.
S20.why: "Prieks jūs atkal redzēt" is a native greeting for someone coming back; "Laipni lūdzam atpakaļ" reads as a translated hotel sign.

S21.why: In a label and value the participle agrees with "vietas", not with the number, so VoiceOver says it correctly for any count.

S22.why: The vocabulary's list title used as a label before the number, so nothing has to agree with 1, 2, 5 or 21; the second sentence needs no noun.

S23.s: Cutling ir atbloķēts. Tagad varat saglabāt līdz %@ Cutlings.
S23.back: Cutling is unlocked. Now you-can save up-to 5000 Cutlings.
S23.why: The app's name takes masculine agreement, as Latvian gives names that end in a consonant; Cutling is the app and Cutlings the items, as the vocabulary has them.

S24.why: Passive with no actor, so nobody is blamed; a title with no full stop.

S25.s: Pašlaik nevar sazināties ar App Store. Mēģiniet vēlreiz pēc brīža.
S25.back: Currently cannot connect with App Store. Try(you-polite) again after a-moment.
S25.why: The impersonal "nevar" keeps the fault away from the person; "pēc brīža" is the ordinary way to say shortly.

S26.why: The App Store is the subject and the verb comes last, which is plain Latvian order for a stated fact.

S27.s: Apple kontā, ar kuru esat pierakstījies šajā ierīcē, nav Cutling pirkuma.
S27.back: In-Apple account, with which you-are signed-in on-this device, there-is-no Cutling purchase.
S27.why: The relative clause "ar kuru esat pierakstījies" is the vocabulary's own wording for the account on a device, kept so the app names it one way.

S28.s: Bezmaksas versijā ietilpst %lld Cutlings. Atbloķējot Cutling vienreiz, varēsiet saglabāt, cik gribat.
S28.back: In-free version fit 5 Cutlings. Unlocking Cutling once, you-will-be-able to-save as-many-as you-want.
S28.why: "ietilpst" says how much a thing holds, which suits Siri saying why a save stopped; "cik gribat" is warmer than "cik vēlaties" and still polite.

S29.why: A compact count, with the same "bez maksas" as S1, so the main screen and the sheet use the same words for free.

K1.why: A headline with "ir" dropped, the way Latvian compresses a short notice; the infinitive "Atbloķēt" names what tapping the capsule does, in the same verb as the button.

M1.why: A verb-led command in the infinitive, the form Latvian Mac menu items and window titles take.

M2.why: The same command as M1, with the ellipsis character because it opens a window.

M3.why: The vocabulary's item word with the attributive "bezmaksas", which here has its noun after it.

M4.why: The number pair Latvians write, with "no" for of; no noun, so nothing has to agree.

M5.why: A status with "ir" dropped, as Latvian settings statuses are written; masculine to agree with the name.

M6.s: Viens pirkums atbloķē Cutling iPhone, iPad un Mac ierīcēs.
M6.back: One purchase unlocks Cutling on-iPhone, iPad and Mac devices.
M6.why: The indeclinable product names are carried by the locative "ierīcēs", the usual Latvian way to put brand names in a case.

M7.s: Cutling ir atbloķēts iPhone, iPad un Mac ierīcēs ar šo Apple kontu.
M7.back: Cutling is unlocked on-iPhone, iPad and Mac devices with this Apple account.
M7.why: The same construction as M6 so the two lines read as before and after; "šo" points at the account shown in Settings.

M8.s: Nopirkāt Cutling, pirms tas kļuva bezmaksas, tāpēc tas paliek atbloķēts. Paldies par to.
M8.back: You-bought Cutling before it became free, therefore it stays unlocked. Thanks for that.
M8.why: The past jūs form "nopirkāt" has no gender, so it fits every buyer; "Paldies par to" thanks them for that purchase in particular.
